page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores running at 4.2 GHz. The memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB RAM, yielding 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2156.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 3991.37 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 26.0 GB/sec fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory read bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached large block reads measuring 36.24 GB/sec and small block cached reads at 310.47 GB/sec, both ranking in the lower performance tier.

From a resource density perspective, the E4ds_v6 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel compute scaling. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage adds value for temporary data caching, though the low multi-core scaling and weak Redis SET performance of 5.66 million operations per second represent clear tradeoffs for highly parallelized or memory-write-heavy database applications.

This server is configured for memory-intensive single-threaded tasks, small-scale database operations, text processing, and lightweight LLM inference, where its prompt processing speed of 436.99 tokens per second for a small 135M model is average. It is less suitable for software compilation or ray tracing due to lower multi-core efficiency.
